children: U.S. stock futures are slipping ahead of a week that will highlight inflation and jobs data.

Just after 6 p.m. Eastern time, Dow Jones Industrial Average futures were down 104 points or 0.2%, while S&P 500 futures were down 0.2% as were Nasdaq 100 futures. Oil futures were up 1% above $93 a barrel.

This week's economic highlights include the release of the personal consumption expenditures price index for August from the Bureau of Economic Analysis on Wednesday and the September jobs report, which the Bureau of Labor Statistics will release Friday.

Economists expect a 3.7% increase in the PCE from a year ago and a 3.3% increase in the core PCE price index, excluding volatile food and energy prices. The consensus among economists is that nonfarm payrolls increased 100,000 in September, while the unemployment rate stayed at 4.1%.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average ended last week up 0.3%, snapping a three-week losing streak and posting its largest one-week point and percentage gain since the week ending Aug. 28, according to Dow Jones Market Data. The Dow is up 7.8% so far this year.

The S&P 500 index ended the week up 1.2%, snapping a two-week losing streak and notching its largest one-week point and percentage increase since the week ending Aug. 7. The S&P 500 is up 13.1% year to date.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite wrapped up the week up 2.1%, also posting its largest one-week point and percentage gain since the week ending Aug. 7. The Nasdaq is up 16.5% this year.
President Donald Trump and Iranian officials traded criticisms over the state of discussions to end the war in Iran.
Trump said Saturday on Fox News that he rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz as "unacceptable."

Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Sunday told NBC News' Meet the Press with Kristen Welker that "there is always hope for diplomacy," adding, "but to be honest with you, we have no reason to come back to diplomacy and engage with this administration once again, because of how they've behaved in the past two years."

U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz told Meet the Press that Trump "will leave all options on the table to ensure the world is safe from Iran holding the world hostage with a nuclear weapon," calling Iranian demands for the end of the U.S. naval blockade and sanctions and the unfreezing of Iranian assets "unacceptable."
Brent crude, the international benchmark, ended Friday up 0.2%, at $97.61 a barrel. West Texas Intermediate, the U.S. benchmark, ended the week at $92.41 a barrel.

Gasoline pump prices were at an average of $4.48 a gallon on Sunday, up from $4.10 a gallon last month and $3.14 a gallon a year ago, according to AAA. Diesel prices were averaging $6.47 a gallon on Sunday, up from $5.62 a gallon last month and $3.69 a gallon a year ago.
